summary: The paper proposes LayerBudget, a training-free online allocator that jointly assigns a per-layer token retention count n_l and a per-layer KV bit-width b_l in {4,8,16} under a global byte budget, solving a multiple-choice-knapsack surrogate greedily by quality-gain-per-byte on a hand-specified objective Q = C(l,n_l) * F(b_l) * w_l (coverage power law, cosine-similarity fidelity constant, sigmoid depth importance). Two auxiliary ideas accompany it: 'quantize first, evict last' and mean-fill of evicted KV positions. Evaluation covers 7 models (7B-72B, MHA and GQA), 17 reimplemented baselines, WikiText-2 PPL at 512-32K, MMLU, GSM8K, NIAH, LongBench-v1, and a small RULER slice, plus HF DynamicCache and vLLM integrations. I like the abstraction: making eviction and quantization commensurable in one currency (Delta Q / Delta M) is the right way to think about this problem, and the paper's honest architecture-dependence finding (early-layer bottleneck on Mistral, late on Llama-2-13B, flat on Qwen2.5-14B) is a genuinely useful negative result. But the paper does not deliver the contribution it bills. Its own component ablation shows the joint allocator gives zero benefit over the trivial 'quantize everything to INT4' alternative at CR<=3x and is 3.2x / 45x WORSE at CR=6x (Component analysis table, A1: Mistral Joint 3.23 vs Quant-only 1.00; Llama-2 45.09 vs 1.01). Across every headline metric -- PPL at 1024 and at 16K/32K, MMLU, NIAH, RULER, LongBench -- LayerBudget ties or loses to the pure-quantization baseline KIVI, which the paper itself concedes ('matches KIVI's PPL within sampling noise at 2-3x'). The one regime where LayerBudget is the only option (CR>4x, beyond the INT4 floor) is exactly the regime where it falls off a cliff. On top of that I found several hard internal contradictions: the 'LayerBudget (Ours)' rows in three zero-fill tables (45.09 on Llama-2, 3.23 on Mistral at 6x) are numerically identical to the ablation's SIGMOID (non-default) importance row, not to the inverted-importance row (2.52 / 1.283) the paper says all results use; the abstract's '<=1.03 at 4x on seven models' is contradicted by Llama-2-13B at 1.11; 'matches Full KV accuracy on every model' on NIAH is contradicted by Mistral 73.3 vs Full 86.7; the fidelity constant Delta F_{4->8}=0.0035 used to justify 'quantize first' is off by 6x from the paper's own calibration table (0.0224); and the memory table reports 24.3% / 42.9% / 71.2% savings for three models all labelled CR=2x while an appendix claims every effective CR matches nominal within +/-0.05. Finally, the operating envelope (2-6x, cliff at 6x) sits 3-7x below the 2026 published bar. This is a good idea reported as if it were a working method.
strengths: The central abstraction is genuinely the right one and is transferable beyond this paper. Making token count and bit-width commensurable through a single marginal-gain-per-byte currency (Delta Q / Delta M over the action set {add_tokens, upgrade_bits}, Section 'Greedy Marginal-Gain Allocation') dissolves the artificial split between the eviction literature and the quantization literature. The derived slogan 'quantize first, evict last' is a crisp, falsifiable design principle that a reader can carry to a different solver, a different objective, or a different hardware bit-width set. Even if this instantiation underdelivers, the framing is the kind of thing that reshapes how people set up the problem.

The architecture-dependence result is a real, useful, and unusually honest negative finding. The paper's flagship heuristic is inverted (early-high) importance, and the paper itself runs the same leave-one-out probe on two more models and reports that the bottleneck direction flips: Llama-2-13B (40L MHA) is late-bottleneck (+0.093 late vs +0.030 early) and Qwen2.5-14B (48L GQA) is flat (+0.039 vs +0.038) (Section 'Ablation Study'). Most submissions would have quietly dropped those two models. This finding -- that 'which layers matter under eviction' is not a property of transformers but of a specific architecture -- is more valuable to the field than the allocator itself, and it directly challenges the fixed-pyramid assumption baked into PyramidKV, MiniKV, and similar work.

Mean-fill is a cheap, general, orthogonal trick with the largest measured effect in the whole paper, and it can be adopted by every eviction method tomorrow at a one-line cost. Filling evicted slots with the mean of retained KV drops logits KL from 0.249 to 0.009 on Mistral-7B at 6x and from 0.6696 to 0.0636 on Llama-2-7B, and takes the Llama-2-7B PPL ratio at 6x from 45.09 to 1.13 (Section 'Analysis'). The paper further reports that median-fill and random-fill (matched moments) work comparably, which correctly identifies the mechanism as first-moment preservation rather than a lucky heuristic. This is the part of the paper I expect to be reused.

The theory section shows genuine discipline where most papers overreach: it explicitly declines the standard (1-1/e) submodular guarantee and explains why (Q = C*F*w is a product, and the marginal-gain ordering over the joint (n_l,b_l) action set shifts when b_l changes, so the action graph is not the required matroid), then states plainly that greedy is used as a fast heuristic against an impractical FPTAS. Declining an available but inapplicable bound is exactly the behaviour I want to reward.

The empirical scaffolding is broad and reported as an envelope rather than a single cherry-picked point: 7 models spanning 7B-72B and both MHA and GQA, 17 reimplemented baselines behind a unified interface, CRs from 1.5x to 8x, context 512 to 32K, a drop-in HuggingFace DynamicCache subclass, and a vLLM LayerBudgetBlockManager that rounds budgets to 16-token PagedAttention blocks. The infrastructure investment is real and the sweep from 1.5x to 8x (Budget sweep table) shows the authors looked for the failure point rather than stopping at the flattering operating point.
weaknesses: FATAL (fatal-flaw gate (a) and probe P12): the paper's own ablation shows the headline contribution -- joint (n_l,b_l) allocation -- has zero marginal value at the CRs it claims and is catastrophically negative beyond them. Component analysis table (A1), PPL ratio, zero-fill: at 3x, Joint (Ours) = 1.00 vs Quant-only = 1.00 on Mistral-7B and 1.02 vs 1.02 on Llama-2-7B (exact ties with the trivial alternative of 'set every layer to INT4 and evict nothing'); at 6x, Joint = 3.23 vs Quant-only = 1.00 on Mistral and 45.09 vs 1.01 on Llama-2. The component that the abstract lists first is measurably worse than deleting it. The A3 rows compound this: {4,16} and {4,8,16} give byte-identical PPL (1.02/45.09 and 1.02/45.09 on Llama-2; 3.23/3.23 on Mistral), so the INT8 rung -- one third of the claimed per-layer precision search space -- has no measurable effect either. FIX REQUIRED: this cannot be closed by prose. Either produce a memory-matched experiment in which joint allocation beats quant-only by a margin exceeding the paper's own quoted PPL std (~2.3 at S=1024), or demote the allocator from contribution 1 to a component and rebill the paper around mean-fill and the architecture-dependence finding, which are the two things with measured effects.

FATAL (fatal-flaw gate (a) and probe P1): LayerBudget ties or loses to KIVI, the fairest strong baseline, on every metric at every scale, and the abstract's ranking claim is gerrymandered to hide this by inventing the category 'token-compression methods' (which excludes KIVI by construction). Evidence, all from the paper's own tables: main PPL table -- Mistral 4x, LB 1.03 vs KIVI 1.01 (KIVI wins); Llama-2-7B 6x, 1.17 vs 1.02 (KIVI wins); Qwen3-8B all CRs, LB 1.00/1.01/1.01/1.03 vs KIVI 1.01 flat (tie/loss). Large-model table -- Llama-2-13B 4x/6x, LB 1.11/1.56 vs KIVI 1.02/1.02. Long-context table -- Mistral 32K 4x, LB 1.009 vs KIVI 1.008 (KIVI wins); Llama-3.1-8B 32K 4x, 1.035 vs 1.035 (tie). MMLU -- LB 47.7/64.1/60.1/72.6/76.1 vs KIVI 47.7/63.7/60.1/72.7/76.6 (KIVI wins 2, ties 2). GSM8K (n=200) -- KIVI wins on Llama-2 (9.0 vs 7.5) and Llama-3.1 (22.0 vs 22.5 is within noise). LongBench -- LB 0.055/0.040/0.050 vs KIVI 0.053/0.041/0.048. Qwen2.5-72B -- PPL tie at 1.00 across 2-4x, RULER@2x KIVI 99 vs LB 98. NIAH is the ONLY place LB is ahead, and only on Llama-2-7B (100 vs 93.3 = one needle out of fifteen) and Mistral@2x (86.7 vs 73.3); on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, Llama-2-13B, Qwen2.5-14B and Qwen2.5-72B both are 100/100. FIX REQUIRED: a new experiment at matched bytes and matched effective-bits-per-token on a benchmark where the gap is larger than the reported noise. As submitted, the honest headline is 'we match INT4 quantization below 4x and lose to it above 4x'.

HARD INTERNAL CONTRADICTION (probe P5) that calls the flagship configuration into question: the 'LayerBudget (Ours)' rows in three separate zero-fill tables are numerically IDENTICAL to the ablation's SIGMOID (late-high) importance row -- the configuration the paper explicitly rejects -- and differ from the inverted (early-high) row the paper says every result uses. Ablation table at 6x: Sigmoid = 3.231 (Mistral) / 45.09 (Llama-2); Inverted = 1.283 / 2.52. Zero-fill PPL table at 6x: LayerBudget = 3.23 (Mistral) / 45.09 (Llama-2). Component analysis A1 at 6x: Joint (Ours) = 3.23 / 45.09. A3 both rows: 3.23 / 45.09. Budget-sweep table at 6x: Combined = 3.23. All five agree with sigmoid to three significant figures and disagree with inverted by 2.5x and 18x. Section 'Method' states 'we report end-to-end results under it [inverted importance] across all models for consistency', and Section 'Analysis' quotes 45.09 as the pre-mean-fill number for the default method. Either the ablation table's Inverted row is not what is deployed, or every zero-fill result in the paper was produced with the wrong importance direction. FIX REQUIRED: state which importance function produced each table and regenerate the inconsistent ones.

ABSTRACT AND INTRO CLAIMS CONTRADICTED BY THE PAPER'S OWN TABLES (probe P5). (i) Abstract: 'achieves PPL ratio <=1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B'. Large-model scaling table: Llama-2-13B at 4x = 1.11 (and 1.56 at 6x). The claim is false for 1 of the 7 models; the parenthetical silently narrows to '13B-72B at GQA' to exclude it. (ii) Section 'Analysis': 'at CR=4x and 4096 tokens, LayerBudget matches Full KV accuracy on every model'. NIAH table: Mistral-7B Full KV = 86.7, LB at 4x = 73.3 -- a 13.4-point drop. (iii) Main-results bullet: 'Among eviction and joint methods, LayerBudget ranks first at every CR on every model'. Main PPL table, Llama-3.1-8B at 6x: MiniKV = 1.07, LayerBudget = 1.08. MiniKV is a joint eviction+quantization method by the paper's own positioning table, and it wins. (iv) Same bullet: 'it outperforms H2O, CAKE, SnapKV, D2O, and Ada-KV' at 'every configuration across all four models in [the main] Table' -- CAKE, D2O and Ada-KV do not appear in that table at all. (v) Contribution 5: 'remains near-lossless (<=1.009)' at 16K-32K; the long-context table shows Llama-3.1-8B at 1.035 at 4x for both 16K and 32K.

THE MEMORY ACCOUNTING IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT AND CONTRADICTS ITS OWN RECONCILIATION APPENDIX (probes P3, P5). In the KV-memory table, all three rows are labelled CR=2x yet the measured savings are 24.3% (Llama-2-7B, 287->218 MB, effective CR 1.32x), 42.9% (Mistral-7B, 95->54 MB, 1.76x) and 71.2% (Llama-3.1-8B, 189->54 MB, 3.50x). None is 2x, and the spread is 0.68 below to 1.50 above nominal -- yet the Byte-CR Reconciliation appendix claims an audit of 1,779 checkpoints confirmed 'every method's effective CR ... matches its nominal CR within +/-0.05'. Worse, Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B are stated in Setup to have IDENTICAL KV geometry (both 32L, 8 KV heads, GQA) yet their reported base KV differs by exactly 2x at every sequence length (189/379/1513 MB vs 95/191/762 MB). Direct computation for that geometry at S=512 with d=128, FP16 gives 2 * 32 * 512 * 8 * 128 * 2 bytes = 67.1 MB, so neither number is right and one is 2.8x too large. Since every 'memory-matched' and CR claim in the paper rests on this accounting, this is not a typo -- it is the measurement instrument. FIX REQUIRED: regenerate all memory numbers from one denominator and re-derive every CR-labelled result.

A LOAD-BEARING CONSTANT IN THE CENTRAL ARGUMENT IS WRONG BY 6x (probe P3). Section 'Theoretical Properties' justifies diminishing fidelity returns -- and thus the whole 'quantize first' ordering -- with 'Delta F_{4->8} = 0.0035 > Delta F_{8->16} = 0.0001'. Recomputing from the paper's own Per-Model Fidelity Calibration table: mean F(4) over the six listed models = (0.9794+0.9758+0.9817+0.9683+0.9781+0.9810)/6 = 0.9774; mean F(8) = (0.9998+0.9997+0.9999+0.9997+0.9998+0.9999)/6 = 0.9998. So Delta F_{4->8} = 0.0224, not 0.0035, and Delta F_{8->16} = 1.0000-0.9998 = 0.0002, not 0.0001. The LayerBudget-KV appendix independently states 'F(8) and F(4) differ by only 0.02', confirming 0.0224 and contradicting the main text. The inequality direction survives, but a paper whose core design principle is derived from a constant it reports 6x wrong has not checked its own arithmetic.

THE BASELINES ARE NOT CREDIBLE, WHICH VOIDS THE PAPER'S MOST QUOTED NUMBERS (probe P4). SnapKV scores 27.1% on MMLU for Llama-2-7B (MMLU chance = 25%) and 29.6/29.4/33.4 on the other models, i.e. the paper reports a widely-used, near-lossless-in-its-own-paper method as producing a model at chance. H2O reaches a PPL ratio of 83.4x at 32K/4x and 34.9x at 16K/4x -- the abstract's most dramatic contrast -- while the H2O paper reports <2% degradation, a discrepancy the authors acknowledge but resolve only by reporting a second broken number (29.4%). Most damning: the LongBench table reports FULL KV (no compression at all) at 0.056 / 0.040 / 0.050 mean F1-ROUGE-L across 16 English tasks, roughly an order of magnitude below published LongBench values, and H2O scoring 0.097 on Llama-2-7B -- nearly 2x the uncompressed model -- explained away as 'degenerate repetition inflating F1'. A harness in which the uncompressed model scores 0.05 and a broken method scores 2x higher is not measuring anything, so 'LayerBudget matches Full KV on all models' on that table is vacuous. Related protocol gap: the profiler extracts the LAST-TOKEN attention row, i.e. query-aware selection, but the paper never states whether compression happens before or after the query is appended -- the 2026 matched-budget audits show this single choice moves rankings by more than most method gaps, and the same is true of the sdpa/eager backend choice, which is stated only for the long-context runs.

THE OBJECTIVE THE ALLOCATOR MAXIMIZES IS NEVER VALIDATED AGAINST THE QUANTITY THE PAPER CARES ABOUT (probe P11). Q = C(l,n_l) * F(b_l) * w_l multiplies an unvalidated power-law coverage guess, a cosine similarity between original and dequantized tensors, and an unnormalized hand-set sigmoid with hyperparameters (k=5, tau=0.3) that the paper admits were tuned on Mistral-7B and do not transfer. The product has no units and no decision-theoretic meaning, and nowhere in the paper is Q shown to correlate with PPL or with any task metric; the only validation offered is that coverage predicts attention mass to 3.1% MAE on one model. w_l in particular is never measured at all -- it is posited. Additionally, the coverage law's premise fails in the deployment regime: heavy hitters are selected from the last-token attention row, but that row changes at every decode step, so C(l,n_l) describes the retained set's coverage for one token only and no experiment measures coverage across multi-step generation. This is a theory/implementation mismatch, not a presentational gap: what is optimized is not shown to be what is evaluated.

THE COMPLEXITY AND LATENCY ARGUMENT CONTRADICTS THE PAPER'S OWN PSEUDOCODE (probes P3, P11). Section 'Greedy Marginal-Gain Allocation' projects Qwen2.5-72B at S=32K as 80 * 32768/8 = 327,680 iterations at ~30 ns each = ~10 ms. The arithmetic of the iteration count is right, but Algorithm 1 places a FOR loop over all L layers and both actions INSIDE the WHILE loop, so each of those 327,680 greedy steps costs an O(L) rescan: 80 * 327,680 = 26.2M candidate evaluations. At 30 ns per evaluation that is 786 ms, not 10 ms; the quoted 30 ns per *iteration* implies 0.19 ns per candidate evaluation, which is below one clock cycle. Combined with the measured 61-109% profiling overhead, the +2.6% to +12.2% TPOT penalty, and the memory table's own footnote ('Speedup <1x due to compression overhead'), the paper's systems story is currently a net slowdown at every measured point.

SIGNIFICANCE: the operating envelope is 3-7x below the current published bar and the related work does not engage the 2026 literature at all (probes P1, P13, P14). LayerBudget's usable range ends at 4x (it cliffs to 1.25-3.23 at 6x), whereas 2026 top-venue results in this exact area report 20x (STAR-KV, ICML 2026 Spotlight, with low-rank-aware mixed-precision quantization), 20-40x (KVTC, ICLR 2026), and 97.81% of full-cache accuracy at 2.48% retention via rate-distortion bit allocation over the SAME joint eviction/quantization action space (RDKV). None of RDKV, HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, public code, the same hybrid quantization+eviction formulation), DefensiveKV / Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026, layer-wise budget allocation, RULER 91.4 at 20% cache), TurboQuant, ThinKV, PolyKV, KVCompose, or NVIDIA's KVPress harness (which already ships PerLayerCompressionPress alongside QuantizedCache -- i.e. a public implementation of this paper's premise) is cited or compared. The benchmark suite is likewise the 2024 suite: WikiText-2 PPL, LongBench-v1 (now dated and here broken), NIAH at 4096, MMLU 0-shot, GSM8K at n=200. LongBench-v2, RULER beyond 4096, InfiniteBench, SCBench, HELMET and the reasoning suite (AIME, MATH-500, GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench) are absent, as is effective-bits-per-token, the common currency the field now reports. A reader cannot place this paper against the state of the art from what is on the page.

SUBMISSION-POLICY AND PRESENTATION DEFECTS THAT ARE DESK-REJECT RISKS (probe P10). (a) The source as submitted does not compile: '\begin{table[t]' (Importance direction ablation) is malformed, '\section{Analysis' has an unclosed brace, '\textbf{Downstream accuracy.' is unclosed, and 'On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~...' has an unclosed parenthesis. As a consequence the Limitations discussion is orphaned inside a broken section and has no heading of its own -- NeurIPS expects an identifiable limitations discussion. (b) The main results table is an 18-column table wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!} on top of \small and tabcolsep=2pt; this shrinks the rendered font well below the NeurIPS style size, and the handbook states that submissions 'violating the NeurIPS style (e.g., by decreasing margins or font sizes) ... may be desk rejected'. (c) The checklist is only an \input{checklist} stub, so the mandatory items -- including the LLM-usage declaration -- cannot be verified as answered, which matters given the machine-generated register flagged in P6. (d) With 3 figures and 3 large tables in the main text plus 8 sections, the 9-content-page limit is at serious risk and cannot be checked from source. (e) Multiple sentences in the abstract, contributions, and results terminate mid-claim at an unescaped percent sign (e.g. 'reducing output distortion by 96\', 'achieving 118--119\'), so the '118-119%' claim central to contribution 1 -- 118-119% of WHAT? a ratio above 100% cannot be a fraction of an optimum -- is literally unverifiable as submitted.

The paper's only mechanism figures characterize a model that appears in no results table (probe P9). The allocation heatmap and the signal-curves figure are both on TinyLlama-1.1B, as is the motivating Gini-spread statistic (0.43-0.93, '2.1x spread') in the Introduction and the rho=0.194 complementarity claim in Section 'Two Complementary Signals'. TinyLlama-1.1B is evaluated nowhere in the paper. So the empirical foundation of the two-signal design and two of the three figures rest on a model outside the evaluated set, while there is no figure of the actual allocation on any evaluated model and no figure of the leave-one-out curves that constitute contribution 2.
questions: Which importance function produced the 'LayerBudget (Ours)' rows in the zero-fill PPL table, the component analysis (A1/A3), and the budget sweep? Those rows read 3.23 (Mistral 6x) and 45.09 (Llama-2 6x), which match the ablation's Sigmoid (late-high) row to three significant figures, while the ablation's Inverted (early-high) row -- the stated default -- reads 1.283 and 2.52. Please state the configuration per table and regenerate any table that was not run with the deployed default. If the default really does give 1.283/2.52, then the component analysis conclusion changes and the mean-fill 45.09 -> 1.13 headline needs restating.

Can you show a single memory-matched, noise-controlled experiment in which joint (n_l,b_l) allocation beats quant-only INT4? Your own A1 rows show an exact tie at 3x and a 3.2x / 45x loss at 6x, and A3 shows the INT8 rung changes nothing. The abstract cites a memory-matched comparison in an appendix that is not present in the submission. Please provide it, with effective bits per token as the common axis, paired bootstrap CIs, and at least one long-context retrieval benchmark (RULER at >=16K or LongBench-v2) rather than WikiText-2 PPL.

What is the empirical relationship between your optimized surrogate Q = C*F*w and the metrics you actually evaluate? A scatter of Q against measured PPL (or task accuracy) across allocations at fixed budget would settle whether the allocator is optimizing the right thing. Relatedly, w_l is a sigmoid with k=5, tau=0.3 that you report is Mistral-tuned and directionally wrong for Llama-2-13B -- how sensitive are the reported results to (k, tau), and what does the per-architecture one-bit LOO probe cost and gain on all seven models?

Is compression query-aware or query-agnostic? Your profiler uses the last-token attention row, which leaks the query into the scoring signal when the question is already in context. Matched-budget audits report that switching to the deployment order (compress the context, then append the question) drops several published methods below a keep-start-plus-recent-window trivial baseline. Please report NIAH and RULER under both protocols, and state the attention backend (sdpa vs eager) for every experiment, not just the long-context ones.

Why do Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B, which you list with identical KV geometry (32 layers, 8 KV heads, GQA), report base KV cache sizes differing by exactly 2x at every sequence length (95/191/762 MB vs 189/379/1513 MB)? And why do three rows all labelled CR=2x show 24.3%, 42.9% and 71.2% measured savings (effective CR 1.32x, 1.76x, 3.50x) when the Byte-CR Reconciliation appendix claims all effective CRs match nominal within +/-0.05 across 1,779 checkpoints?

Why does Full KV score 0.056 / 0.040 / 0.050 on LongBench with no compression applied, and why does H2O score 0.097 on Llama-2-7B -- nearly double the uncompressed model? Similarly, why is SnapKV at 27.1% MMLU on Llama-2-7B, i.e. chance level? Until these are explained, 'LayerBudget matches Full KV' on LongBench and the 83x H2O collapse at 32K cannot be read as evidence about the methods rather than about the harness.

How does LayerBudget compare against the 2026 joint eviction+quantization line -- RDKV's rate-distortion reverse-water-filling allocation, HqeKV (public code), DefensiveKV/Layer-DefensiveKV, KVTC, STAR-KV -- and why did you not build on or evaluate within NVIDIA's KVPress, which already exposes PerLayerCompressionPress together with QuantizedCache? These report 14x-40x operating points while your method cliffs at 6x; what is the argument that the 2-4x regime is still the interesting one?

probe_answers.answer: Five-plus plausible alternatives. (1) KIVI / plain uniform INT4 quantization -- COMPARED head-to-head in every table, and it ties or beats LayerBudget nearly everywhere (Mistral 4x 1.01 vs 1.03; Llama-2-7B 6x 1.02 vs 1.17; Llama-2-13B 4x/6x 1.02/1.02 vs 1.11/1.56; MMLU KIVI wins 2 of 5; Qwen2.5-72B RULER@2x 99 vs 98; long-context Mistral 32K 4x 1.008 vs 1.009). The paper's rebuttal is that KIVI caps at ~4x and loses on NIAH, but the NIAH advantage exists on only 2 of 7 models and is one needle out of fifteen on Llama-2-7B. (2) 'Quantize everything to INT4, evict nothing' -- the paper's own Quant-only ablation row. It TIES the full method at 3x and beats it by 3.2x/45x at 6x. An alternative that the paper implements and loses to. (3) NVIDIA KVPress -- the de-facto public harness with 30+ methods, a HuggingFace leaderboard, and built-in PerLayerCompressionPress plus QuantizedCache, i.e. an existing public implementation of per-layer compression composed with a quantized cache. IGNORED ENTIRELY -- never cited, never used, and the 17 baselines are all self-reimplemented instead, which is precisely how one gets SnapKV at chance-level MMLU. (4) RDKV (rate-distortion bit allocation for joint eviction+quantization, reverse water-filling with Lagrangian relaxation, training-free, TriZone packed-decode kernel; 97.81% of full-cache accuracy at 2.48% retention on LongBench, 4.5x decode speedup at 128K) -- the closest possible competitor, occupying the identical action space with a principled solver instead of a hand-tuned surrogate. IGNORED ENTIRELY. (5) HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, public code, hybrid quantization+eviction with an integrated per-element optimizer and a joint K-V importance metric) -- IGNORED. (6) DefensiveKV / Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026, layer-wise budget allocation, RULER 39.0 -> 91.4 at 20% cache), STAR-KV (ICML 2026 Spotlight, 20x with low-rank-aware mixed-precision), KVTC (ICLR 2026, 20-40x), TurboQuant, ThinKV, PolyKV, KVCompose -- all IGNORED. The only 2026 works engaged are MoE-nD and xKV, and both comparisons use the authors' own reimplementations because 'the official artifacts were not public'. Ignoring KVPress and RDKV in particular is a fatal weakness: one is the standard harness the community would have run this in, the other solves the same problem better with a real derivation.

(1) Compression ratio / CR -- overloaded four ways: nominal CR, byte CR against FP16 full cache (Section 'CR definition'), token-count CR ('method-byte CR diverges from token-count CR'), and allocator-side CR which the Byte-CR appendix admits is inflated 2x. The paper needs a whole appendix to reconcile its own central axis, and even then the memory table's rows labelled CR=2x measure 1.32x/1.76x/3.50x. (2) S -- introduced as sequence length in the Introduction, then used in the coverage law C=(n_l/S)^{1-g_l} where it must mean the full prompt length at profiling time, then again in the allocator's iteration bound and in table headers as 'seq'. During decoding S grows, and which S the coverage law refers to is never resolved. (3) Layer index l -- the objective sums l=1..L but the importance function is w_l = sigma(k(1 - l/(L-1) - tau)), which is the 0-indexed form; at l=L the term l/(L-1) exceeds 1 and w_l goes below the intended floor. One-off indexing error in the only closed-form the method defines. (4) n_min -- 'sink + recent', but the number of sink tokens and the recent-window size are never given anywhere in the paper, so the minimum allocation (and hence the achievable CR) is unspecified and the method is not reproducible from the text. (5) B and B_used -- 'total memory budget' with no units and no stated mapping from a target CR to B; B_used appears only in Algorithm 1 and is never defined. (6) Q -- called 'quality', but it is a dimensionless product of a probability-like coverage, a cosine similarity, and an unnormalized sigmoid; its scale is arbitrary and it is never related to any measured quality. (7) '118--119%' (contribution 1 and Section 'Theoretical Properties') -- 118-119% of what reference is truncated away; no denominator is ever stated, and a value above 100% cannot be a fraction of the MCKP optimum. (8) F(b) 'fidelity' -- defined as mean cosine similarity, but why quality should be MULTIPLICATIVE in a cosine similarity is never argued. (9) 'LB' vs 'LayerBudget' vs 'LB-KV' vs 'LayerBudget-KV' -- used interchangeably across table rows without a stated equivalence. (10) 'the MoE-nD framing' -- a term coined in this paper for a reimplementation of someone else's method; it appears in table rows as if it were a method name.

Three recomputations; two fail. (A) FIDELITY DELTAS (the constant that justifies 'quantize first'). Section 'Theoretical Properties' asserts Delta F_{4->8} = 0.0035 > Delta F_{8->16} = 0.0001. From the paper's own Per-Model Fidelity Calibration table: F(4) values 0.9794, 0.9758, 0.9817, 0.9683, 0.9781, 0.9810 sum to 5.8643, mean = 0.97738. F(8) values 0.9998, 0.9997, 0.9999, 0.9997, 0.9998, 0.9999 sum to 5.9988, mean = 0.99980. Therefore Delta F_{4->8} = 0.99980 - 0.97738 = 0.02242, and Delta F_{8->16} = 1.00000 - 0.99980 = 0.00020. The paper's stated 0.0035 is 6.4x too small and its 0.0001 is 2x too small. The LayerBudget-KV appendix independently says 'F(8) and F(4) differ by only 0.02', confirming my number and contradicting the main text. DOES NOT CHECK OUT. (B) KV MEMORY. Setup lists Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B as both 32L, 8 KV heads, GQA. FP16 KV bytes = 2 (K and V) * L * S * H_kv * d * 2 bytes. At S=512, d=128: 2*32*512*8*128*2 = 67,108,864 bytes = 67.1 MB. The memory table reports 95 MB for Mistral and 189 MB for Llama-3.1-8B at S=512 -- identical geometry, 2.0x apart, and neither equals the computed value. The 2x ratio holds exactly at 1024 (191 vs 379) and 4096 (762 vs 1513). DOES NOT CHECK OUT. (C) EFFECTIVE CR IN THAT SAME TABLE, all rows labelled CR=2x: 287/218 = 1.317x (24.3% saved, matches their 24.3%), 95/54 = 1.759x (42.9%), 189/54 = 3.500x (71.2%). None is 2x; deviations are -0.68, -0.24, +1.50 against the Byte-CR appendix's claim of +/-0.05 over 1,779 audited checkpoints. DOES NOT CHECK OUT. (D) One that DOES check: allocator iteration count for Qwen2.5-72B at S=32K, 80 * 32768/8 = 80*4096 = 327,680, and 327,680 * 30 ns = 9.83 ms ~ '~10 ms' as claimed. But the projection is still wrong at the algorithmic level: Algorithm 1 rescans all L layers and 2 actions inside the WHILE loop, so total candidate evaluations = 80 * 327,680 = 26.2M, and 30 ns per greedy step implies 0.19 ns per candidate evaluation -- faster than one clock cycle. Corrected at 30 ns per evaluation the projection is ~786 ms, ~80x the stated figure. (E) Consistency checks that DO pass: KL reduction 1 - 0.009/0.249 = 96.4% ~ '96%'; 1 - 0.0636/0.6696 = 90.5% as stated; importance-direction gains 1 - 1.283/3.231 = 60.3% and 1 - 2.52/45.09 = 94.4%, matching '60--94%' -- though these are percentage reductions of a PPL RATIO relative to the authors' own worst variant, which is not a meaningful improvement metric.

Yes on both counts. The two most quotable numbers in the abstract both rest on baselines that are almost certainly misconfigured, and the most favourable framing is not the honest one. (1) 'At 32K context on Mistral-7B, H2O at 4x collapses (83x PPL) while LayerBudget maintains 1.009x'. An 83.4x PPL ratio (and 34.9x at 16K) is not a degradation, it is a broken implementation; the H2O paper reports <2% degradation. The authors pre-empt this with a footnote claiming a 'faithful per-head H2O ... gives 29.4%' on MMLU -- but 29.4% on MMLU is also chance-adjacent, so the verification consists of a second implausible number. (2) SnapKV at 27.1 / 29.6 / 29.4 / 33.4 / 41.2 on MMLU where Full KV is 47.3 / 63.9 / 60.2 / 72.9 / 76.6: SnapKV is being reported at chance on Llama-2. Published SnapKV is near-lossless at these budgets; the likely cause is the query-visibility protocol (SnapKV's observation-window voting depends on the query being visible, and the 2026 matched-budget audit measures SnapKV's query-leakage delta at +0.198), which the paper never specifies. (3) The LongBench table's Full KV row at 0.056/0.040/0.050 shows the harness is broken with NO compression applied, and H2O at 0.097 beats the uncompressed model. (4) Full KV NIAH on Mistral-7B is 86.7% -- the uncompressed model fails 13% of needles at 4096 tokens, so the NIAH instrument itself is weak, and with 15-30 cells per condition the granularity (6.7 points) exceeds most of the reported gaps. (5) The abstract's ranking claim is gerrymandered: 'ranks first among token-compression methods' defines a category that excludes KIVI by construction -- the one baseline that ties or beats the method everywhere. The honest headline is 'matches uniform INT4 below 4x and loses to it above 4x'. (6) Within the ablations, the 60-94% improvement from inverted importance is measured against the sigmoid variant at 3.231 and 45.09 PPL ratio -- the authors' own catastrophically-configured alternative, not against a neutral default; against the Flat (uniform) row the gain at 4x is 0.002-0.065, i.e. nil.

Seven direct self-contradictions. (1) FLAGSHIP CONFIG: the ablation table gives Inverted (the stated default) at 6x as 1.283 (Mistral) / 2.52 (Llama-2) and Sigmoid (explicitly rejected) as 3.231 / 45.09. Yet the zero-fill PPL table, the component analysis A1 'Joint (Ours)' row, both A3 rows, and the budget-sweep 'Combined' column all report 3.23 / 45.09 for the method at 6x -- the sigmoid numbers. Method section: 'we report end-to-end results under it [inverted importance] across all models for consistency.' Both cannot be true. (2) ABSTRACT vs LARGE-MODEL TABLE: '<=1.03 at 4x on seven models' vs Llama-2-13B = 1.11 at 4x. (3) TEXT vs NIAH TABLE: 'matches Full KV accuracy on every model (100%...)' vs Mistral-7B Full 86.7, LB@4x 73.3. (4) TEXT vs MAIN TABLE: 'ranks first at every CR on every model' vs MiniKV 1.07 < LayerBudget 1.08 on Llama-3.1-8B at 6x; and 'it outperforms H2O, CAKE, SnapKV, D2O, and Ada-KV [in that table]' when CAKE, D2O and Ada-KV are not in that table. (5) CONTRIBUTION 5 vs LONG-CONTEXT TABLE: 'remains near-lossless (<=1.009)' at 16K-32K vs Llama-3.1-8B at 1.035 at 4x for both lengths. (6) THEORY vs CALIBRATION APPENDIX: Delta F_{4->8} = 0.0035 vs 0.0224 computed from the paper's own table and 'differ by only 0.02' in the LB-KV appendix. (7) MEMORY TABLE vs BYTE-CR APPENDIX: rows labelled CR=2x measure effective 1.32x / 1.76x / 3.50x, against the appendix's audited '+/-0.05' claim; plus Mistral and Llama-3.1-8B, stated to have identical KV geometry, differ 2x in base KV at every length. Bonus (8): the same Llama-2-7B 6x configuration appears as 1.099 (head-to-head table), 1.13 (Analysis, mean-fill), and 1.17 (main results table, caption says mean-fill) -- three values, differing sequence lengths, never reconciled. Bonus (9): the Related Work presents LayerBudget-KV as the answer to the 6x regime and 'complementary operating regimes of the same framework', while Limitation 5 reports that same variant collapses 4K NIAH retrieval to 26.7% -- a variant that cannot retrieve is not an operating regime.

Yes -- the register is strongly machine-generated, and specifically it reads like text written to pre-empt a reviewer rather than to inform one. (a) Defensive 'not X but Y' parallelisms saturate the captions and appendices: 'the value is the measured ratio (not a typo)'; 'is allocator overhead, not a CR-denominator inconsistency between methods'; 'so the flat ~1.03 PPL across moderate CR is not solver degeneracy'; 'are therefore best read as complementary operating regimes of the same framework rather than two competing solvers'; 'This is not a universal principle'. Captions in a paper should describe the table; these argue with an imagined objection. (b) Promissory reviewer-directed language embedded in the body: 'we will update against their official code at camera-ready' and 'For the camera-ready we will regenerate Table X using mean_memory_bytes as the denominator' -- an entire appendix (Byte-CR Reconciliation) exists only to concede and defer a bookkeeping error. (c) The MoE-nD paragraph in Related Work is a single ~400-word block that abandons the section's rhythm to litigate a head-to-head loss ('only on Mistral-7B at CR=6x does the MoE-nD framing win at this design point'), then introduces a new method variant to cover it. That is a rebuttal, pasted into a related-work section. (d) Uniform bullet rhythm in 'Key findings' -- six bullets, each an assertive topic sentence followed by exactly the supporting numbers, with no bullet reporting a disconfirming result even though the tables contain several. (e) Describing rather than arguing: 'These results validate the Gini stability finding from Section X' where no Gini-stability experiment exists anywhere in the paper -- the sentence performs validation without performing an experiment.

(a) OVER-ASSERTION. 'Nearly all existing methods apply their strategy uniformly across layers' -- contradicted by the paper's own next section, which lists PyramidKV, D2O, SqueezeAttention, CAKE, Ada-KV, EvolKV and LAVa as per-layer or per-head. 'All evict tokens at full precision---none jointly optimize quantization' -- stated as a universal in the same section that describes MiniKV, EVICPRESS, MoE-nD and 'No Token Left Behind' doing exactly that. 'LayerBudget ranks 1st among all token-compression methods' and 'ranks first at every CR on every model' -- falsified by MiniKV at 1.07 vs 1.08 in the paper's own table. 'attention sparsity profiles calibrated at short context transfer to 32K tokens without recalibration' -- asserted from downstream PPL agreement; no Gini-vs-context measurement appears anywhere. 'To our knowledge, no prior online, training-free method jointly optimizes per-layer (n_l,b_l)' -- an aggressive universal given RDKV and HqeKV. Honest forms would be 'most', 'of the methods we surveyed', 'in our reimplementation'. (b) VAGUE REFERENT. 'These results validate the Gini stability finding from Section X' -- 'these results' are PPL ratios, which cannot validate a stability claim about Gini. 'This is intrinsic to the byte budget' (component analysis caption) -- 'this' = quant-only dominating joint, three sentences earlier. 'The reduction generalizes' (Analysis) -- reduction of KL or of PPL ratio? The sentence then gives a KL number and the next gives a PPL number. 'it autonomously avoids eviction' -- 'it' = the joint approach, but the nearest noun is 'quant-only quality'. 'The two design points are therefore best read as complementary operating regimes' -- which two, of the three variants just discussed. (c) THING-VS-PROCESS. 'allocation' denotes both the artifact (the per-layer plan {(n_l,b_l)}) and the procedure ('greedy marginal-gain allocation', 'per allocation'); 'profiling' denotes both the measurement pass and its cost ('The full profiling pipeline adds 61--109%'); 'compression ratio' denotes the target, the achieved byte ratio, the token-count ratio, and the allocator-side ratio; 'importance' denotes both the sigmoid weight w_l and the empirical LOO sensitivity, which the paper shows are not the same thing. (d) FALSE PRECISION. 'reduces output KL divergence by 96%' -- one model, one CR, one fill strategy, reported to two figures. 'improve 6x compression by 60--94%' -- a two-model range presented as an interval, and it is a percentage reduction of a PPL RATIO measured against the authors' own worst variant. '118--119%' -- a 1-point range on an undefined denominator. 'Decode latency remains within 3--5%' -- the same table reports +12.2% on Qwen2.5-14B, so the honest statement is 'within 3-5% on four of five models, 12% on the fifth'. 'MAE 3.1%' -- one model. 'we audited 1,779 PPL checkpoints and confirmed ... within +/-0.05' -- precise-sounding, and contradicted by the paper's own memory table.

THESIS (one sentence): 'Because attention sparsity and eviction sensitivity vary across transformer layers, a greedy per-layer allocator that spends the memory budget on quantization before eviction gives near-lossless KV compression at 2-4x.' Topic sentences that map to the thesis and whose evidence maps to them: the two-family framing; 'The uniform assumption'; 'Our insight: quantize first, evict last'; the problem formulation; the coverage/fidelity/importance decomposition; the greedy allocator; the main PPL results; the long-context results; mean-fill. PARAGRAPHS THAT MAP TO NEITHER (deletion candidates, not revision candidates): (1) The MoE-nD block in Related Work. Its topic sentence is 'The closest concurrent work is MoE-nD', but its evidence is a head-to-head loss at 6x plus the introduction of an entirely new method variant (LayerBudget-KV) that appears nowhere else in the main text. It argues priority, not position. (2) The 'Weak correlation enables complementary allocation' paragraph. Topic sentence claims the two signals are complementary; evidence is rho=0.194 on TinyLlama-1.1B, a model that appears in no results table, and no experiment anywhere tests whether the combination beats Gini alone at the same budget (the budget-sweep table compares combined vs importance-only, never vs Gini-only). (3) The Byte-CR Reconciliation appendix in its entirety. Its topic sentence is 'This appendix reconciles two memory denominators that appear in the paper' -- it exists to manage an internal accounting error and promises to fix it at camera-ready. Its presence IS the finding. (4) 'Theoretical Properties'. The topic sentence would be 'The objective is an instance of MCKP', but the paragraph's content is a list of guarantees that do NOT hold; it maps to the thesis only as a disclaimer, and the one empirical claim in it ('118-119%') has no denominator. (5) The Limitations list has no identifiable topic sentence and no heading at all -- it is orphaned inside a malformed '\section{Analysis' whose brace is never closed, so the reverse outline cannot even place it. A paragraph I could not assign a topic sentence to is itself the finding, and here it is a required NeurIPS element.

I have only the LaTeX source, not a compiled PDF, so ppl_scaling.pdf, allocation_heatmap.pdf and signal_curves.pdf are UNVERIFIABLE as rendered -- I flag that explicitly and cannot certify their correctness. What I CAN check from source is damning enough. (1) Two of the three figures (allocation_heatmap, signal_curves) are on TinyLlama-1.1B, a model that appears in NO results table anywhere in the paper. The paper's only visual account of its own mechanism -- how the allocator actually distributes tokens and bits across layers, and the claimed complementarity of the two signals -- is therefore demonstrated exclusively on a model outside the evaluated set. (2) There is consequently no figure showing the per-layer allocation on any of the seven evaluated models, which is the single most informative artifact this method could produce. (3) There is no figure for contribution 2 (the leave-one-out architecture-dependence finding); it is conveyed only by four numbers in prose (+0.093/+0.030 and +0.039/+0.038), so a reader cannot see the LOO curves that the flagship inverted-importance default is derived from. (4) Three figures total for a 9-page systems paper with 9 main-text-or-appendix tables is an unusually figure-poor presentation of an inherently spatial idea (a budget distributed over depth). (5) The document as given would not compile to a PDF at all (see P10), so no reviewer could have inspected the rendered figures either.

(a) ANONYMITY: I find no institution, author name, funding acknowledgment, or identifying self-citation; author block is 'Anonymous Author(s)'. Two soft issues: 'we will update against their official code at camera-ready' and 'For the camera-ready we will regenerate Table X' are forward references to a post-acceptance state inside the submission body -- not a de-anonymization, but they read as correspondence with reviewers rather than as paper text and should be removed. The priority claim 'To our knowledge, no prior online, training-free method jointly optimizes per-layer (n_l,b_l) across the model architectures and operating regimes we evaluate' is aggressively hedged into unfalsifiability and is contradicted by RDKV and HqeKV. NOT a desk-reject item. (b) COMPLETENESS: the checklist is present only as '\input{checklist}', so no checklist item can be verified as answered -- including the mandatory NeurIPS LLM-usage declaration, which matters given the register flagged in P6. UNVERIFIABLE = risk. (c) FORMAT -- MULTIPLE DESK-REJECT RISKS. (i) The source does not compile: '\begin{table[t]' (Importance direction ablation) is malformed; '\section{Analysis' has an unclosed brace; '\textbf{Downstream accuracy.' is unclosed; 'On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~[REF]' has an unclosed parenthesis and the sentence never terminates. (ii) As a consequence the Limitations discussion has no section heading and is swallowed by the broken '\section{Analysis'. (iii) The main results table is 18 columns wrapped in \resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{} ON TOP OF \small and \tabcolsep=2pt; this reduces the rendered font far below the NeurIPS style size, and the handbook states submissions 'violating the NeurIPS style (e.g., by decreasing margins or font sizes) ... may be desk rejected'. This is the clearest desk-reject exposure in the paper. (iv) Page count cannot be verified from source, but 8 sections plus 3 figures plus 3 large main-text tables puts the 9-content-page limit at real risk. (v) Numerous sentences terminate at unescaped percent signs in the abstract, contributions, and results ('by 96\', 'achieving 118--119\', 'GQA models achieve 43--72\'), leaving several headline claims literally incomplete in the submitted text.

(a) WHAT THE ALGORITHM ACTUALLY COMPUTES: Algorithm 1 initializes every layer at (n_min = sink+recent, b_min = 4) and repeatedly applies the (layer, action) maximizing Delta Q / Delta M, where Q = C(l,n_l) * F(b_l) * w_l with C = (n_l/S)^{1-g_l}, F(b) = mean cosine similarity between original and dequantized K,V over 8 calibration prompts, w_l = sigma(5*(1 - l/(L-1) - 0.3)), and M(n,b) = 2*n*H*d*b/8. So the implementation maximizes a hand-specified scalar surrogate under a byte constraint. (b) DOES THAT EQUAL WHAT THE THEORY NAMES? No. The theory calls Q 'quality', and the paper's evaluation measures PPL, MMLU, NIAH, GSM8K and LongBench. Nowhere is Q shown to correlate with ANY of them. The only validation offered is that C predicts attention mass to 3.1% MAE on one model -- attention mass is not quality. F is a cosine similarity between tensors, not a quality; w is never measured at all, it is posited, and the paper itself reports its direction is wrong on Llama-2-13B. A greedy solver optimizing an unvalidated surrogate is not 'per-layer token-precision joint OPTIMIZATION' in the sense the title claims. (c) SEMANTICS SILENTLY CHANGED: (i) The MCKP framing borrows the vocabulary of a solved combinatorial problem, but the paper concedes the greedy has no approximation guarantee here (not a matroid, product objective) and the FPTAS is impractical -- so what is 'formalized' in contribution 1 is a formulation the paper does not solve and does not bound. (ii) The coverage law's premise fails in deployment: heavy hitters are chosen from the LAST-TOKEN attention row, so C(l,n_l) is the coverage of the retained set for exactly one query. During generation the attention row changes at every decode step and the retained set is stale, yet no experiment measures coverage or quality drift across multi-step generation -- the load-bearing assumption is unjustified for the real setting. (iii) Using the last-token row also makes the selection QUERY-AWARE when the question is already in context, which is not the deployment order; the paper never states which order it uses, and this single choice is known to move retrieval rankings by more than most method gaps. (iv) The latency projection contradicts the algorithm box: 327,680 greedy steps each rescanning L=80 layers x 2 actions = 26.2M evaluations, so the quoted '~30 ns per iteration -> ~10 ms' implies 0.19 ns per evaluation, below one clock cycle. (v) The importance function uses 0-indexed depth l/(L-1) while the objective sums l=1..L. What is proved and what is run do not line up.

CLAIMED CONTRIBUTIONS IN ORDER, each with its isolating experiment and measured marginal effect. C1 'formalize per-layer (n_l,b_l) allocation and propose a quantize-first greedy solver' -- ISOLATING EXPERIMENT: Component analysis (A1). MEASURED EFFECT: at 3x, Joint 1.00 vs Quant-only 1.00 (Mistral) and 1.02 vs 1.02 (Llama-2) = EXACTLY ZERO; at 6x, Joint 3.23 vs Quant-only 1.00 and 45.09 vs 1.01 = STRONGLY NEGATIVE (3.2x and 45x worse than the trivial alternative). The A3 precision-level ablation adds that {4,16} and {4,8,16} are identical to three figures everywhere, so the INT8 rung -- a third of the claimed search space -- contributes nothing. C2 'inverted importance / early-layer bottleneck' -- ISOLATING EXPERIMENT: Importance direction ablation. MEASURED EFFECT vs the neutral Flat baseline: at 4x (inside the claimed operating regime) 1.008 vs 1.010 on Mistral and 1.002 vs 1.067 on Llama-2 -- 0.002 to 0.065, at or below the paper's own noise; the large 60-94% gains are computed against the SIGMOID variant and only materialize at 6x, a regime where quant-only beats the whole method anyway. And the paper itself shows the direction is wrong for Llama-2-13B and absent for Qwen2.5-14B. C3 'mean-fill' -- ISOLATING EXPERIMENT: Analysis section. MEASURED EFFECT: KL 0.249 -> 0.009 and PPL ratio 45.09 -> 1.13 on Llama-2-7B at 6x. BY FAR THE LARGEST EFFECT IN THE PAPER -- and the paper concedes median-fill and random-fill work comparably, so the mechanism is generic first-moment preservation, adoptable by any eviction method, orthogonal to the allocator. C4 '17-baseline controlled comparison' -- not a method contribution, and the baselines are implausible (P4). C5 '16K-32K validation' -- the effect is carried entirely by an H2O number (83x) that no H2O paper reports; against KIVI the margin at 32K/4x is 1.009 vs 1.008, i.e. a loss. C6 'scale to 72B' -- LB 1.00 vs KIVI 1.00 at 4x, NIAH 100 vs 100, RULER@2x 98 vs 99. No marginal benefit. RANKING BY MEASURED MARGINAL EFFECT: mean-fill (huge) >> importance direction (only at 6x, only on 2 of 4 tested models, and directionally wrong on a third) >> joint allocation (zero at <=3x, strongly negative at 6x). RANKING IMPLIED BY THE ABSTRACT: joint allocation first, importance second, mean-fill third. THE ORDERINGS ARE INVERTED. The component billed as primary has an isolating experiment showing it is worse than deleting it. Per the probe's own rule this is a FATAL defect, and the honest fix is to demote C1 and rebill the paper around mean-fill plus the architecture-dependence finding.

(a) ONE SENTENCE IN THE COMMUNITY'S VOCABULARY: 'A training-free, online per-layer budget allocator that jointly chooses KV token retention and mixed-precision bit-width by greedy marginal-gain-per-byte on a hand-specified quality surrogate.' That is statable, so the paper is not mis-scoped -- it belongs in the efficient-inference track of NeurIPS / ICLR / MLSys. Venue fit is NOT the problem here. (b) TERMS A PC MEMBER WOULD HAVE TO LOOK UP because they are coined in this paper and several are used before definition: 'coverage law', 'fidelity constant F(b)', 'inverted importance', 'mean-fill', 'signal crossover', 'the MoE-nD framing', 'quantize first, evict last', 'allocator-side accounting'. Standard vocabulary the paper should be using instead exists: rate-distortion bit allocation, effective bits per token, memory-matched budget, query-aware vs query-agnostic compression. (c) NO mechanism belongs to a different community. The systems half (vLLM BlockManager, TPOT, PagedAttention block rounding) gestures at MLSys, but the systems evidence is negative -- the memory table's own footnote says 'Speedup <1x due to compression overhead' and TPOT overhead reaches +12.2% -- so MLSys would reject it on its own terms. (d) RELATED WORK POSITIONS AGAINST THE WRONG YEAR, which is the real venue problem. It engages the 2024-2025 canon (H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, KIVI, KVQuant, StreamingLLM) plus two 2026 arXiv works it reimplemented itself, and does not cite or compare against the 2026 top-venue bar in its own area: STAR-KV (ICML 2026 Spotlight, 20x), KVTC (ICLR 2026, 20-40x), DefensiveKV / Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026, layer-wise allocation, RULER 39.0 -> 91.4 at 20% cache), TurboQuant (ICLR 2026), RDKV (rate-distortion joint eviction+quantization, 97.81% at 2.48% retention), HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, public code), ThinKV, PolyKV, KVCompose, or the KVPress harness. Its benchmarks are the 2024 set (WikiText-2 PPL, LongBench-v1, NIAH@4096, MMLU 0-shot, GSM8K n=200) rather than LongBench-v2 / RULER at length / InfiniteBench / SCBench / AIME-MATH-500. So this is not a good paper in the wrong room; it is a paper written for this room two years ago, whose headline operating point (4x, cliff at 6x) is 3-10x below what the room now publishes. For the Visionary brief, that is the significance verdict: correct venue, obsolete frontier.

(a) EXPECTED vs PRESENT. Perplexity: REPORTED (WikiText-2, 6 chunks, 512-32K). Long-context retrieval at realistic length (RULER 4K-128K, 13 subtasks): effectively OMITTED -- RULER appears only on Qwen2.5-72B at 4096 with two CRs and no subtask breakdown. LongBench-v2: OMITTED (v1 only, and the v1 harness is broken -- Full KV scores 0.056/0.040/0.050). InfiniteBench / SCBench / HELMET: OMITTED. Reasoning suite (AIME 2024/25, MATH-500, GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench): OMITTED -- GSM8K only, n=200, and on Llama-2 Full KV scores 5.5% so the comparison has no headroom. NIAH: REPORTED but at 4096 only, with Full KV itself at 86.7% on Mistral. MMLU: REPORTED (0-shot, 1140 questions). Effective bits per token, now the common currency: OMITTED entirely. Throughput / decode speedup / peak memory at long context: REPORTED AND NEGATIVE (speedup <1x per the memory table footnote; TPOT +2.6% to +12.2%; profiling overhead 61-109%). Error bars / significance: essentially OMITTED -- one paired-bootstrap CI is referenced in prose but never shown, no table carries intervals, and the paper's own quoted PPL std ~2.3 at S=1024 exceeds many of the differences it calls wins. Memory-matched comparison: CITED IN THE ABSTRACT, APPENDIX ABSENT. (b) OMITTED METRICS THAT COULD REVERSE A CLAIM: effective bits/token and a memory-matched RULER/LongBench-v2 evaluation directly test the abstract's 'ranks first ... at memory-matched comparison', and the supporting appendix does not exist in the submission -- so the headline claim currently has no evidence at all. Throughput is already reversed by the paper's own footnote. (c) UNMEASURED TERMS IN THE PAPER'S OWN OBJECTIVE: all three factors of Q = C*F*w. C is validated only as attention-mass prediction on one model; F is a tensor cosine similarity never related to output quality; w is never measured anywhere -- it is a posited sigmoid whose direction the paper's own LOO probe contradicts on 2 of 3 tested architectures. An objective whose every term is unmeasured against the evaluated metric is a defect independent of field convention. (d) WORKLOAD-REGIME MISMATCH: the motivation is long-context memory pressure (Llama-2-70B at 8K = 40 GB), but the main results table is at S=1024, the ablations at S=512, NIAH at 4096, and only one model reaches 32K. Moreover every model is run with 4-BIT WEIGHTS, which is not the FP16 setting the 40 GB motivating calculation assumes and which plausibly perturbs the attention sparsity profiles the whole method is built on -- an interaction the paper never tests.
